name: Learn a few ballroom dance steps
blurb: A basic waltz box step and a foxtrot will carry you through any wedding. Frame and lead-follow mechanics matter more than footwork.
steps: Learn the frame: upper body held, elbows up, connection through the whole arm rather than the hands. This is how the lead is actually communicated.
Learn the waltz box step, counting 1-2-3 out loud, first alone and then with a partner.
Learn the rise and fall that makes a waltz look like a waltz rather than a walk.
Learn a basic foxtrot: slow, slow, quick, quick, in a smooth travelling line.
Learn to navigate the floor — moving anticlockwise, avoiding collisions, adjusting stride to the space.
Practise with several partners; leading and following one person only builds a private dialect.
tips: Leading is not steering with the hands. It comes from the body and the frame.
Following is not passive. It is active listening through the frame.
Look up and at your partner, not down at your feet.
proof: You dance a full waltz and a full foxtrot with an unfamiliar partner, in time, without collisions.
